editions.label: 24 Oct
editions.title: House prices keep climbing 18.4% even as sales fall 9%
editions.summary: Portugal's housing market is pulling apart. INE's Q2 numbers show prices up 18.4% year-on-year to a median €2,445/m², even as transactions fell 9% to 37,854 — the clearest sign yet that buyers are priced out faster than they walk away. The cooling is uneven: volumes dropped in 22 of 26 sub-regions, steepest in Madeira (-17.9%) and metropolitan Porto (-16.2%), yet prices rose in every one. Lisbon's own sales slid 9.3% while its median held at €4,030/m². Against that squeeze, the government's OE2027 earmarks €2,003 million to push supply, the largest slice to public housing and rehabilitation. Meanwhile the capital that is moving is chasing trophies — Penha Longa at €140M, a €220M AI data centre in Coruche — even as broad M&A dries up. Net: the gap between what Portugal costs and what it can absorb is the story of 2027, and smart money is already positioning around it.
editions.hook: Fewer homes change hands — for ever more money.

items.headline: Penha Longa resort sells for €140M to Catterton and Cedar Capital
items.summary: The five-star Caesar Park hotel and golf resort in Sintra is among the few large Portuguese transactions still closing, bought by Catterton Management and Cedar Capital Partners as the broader deal market thins.
items.why: Trophy hospitality is where international capital is concentrating — proof the appetite is selective, not gone.

items.headline: The Lince Hotels buys Villa Garden in Braga for a five-star makeover
items.summary: Arliz group's hospitality arm acquires the 26-room hotel set in a 19th-century palace, with works to lift it to five stars starting in 2027. Price undisclosed.
items.why: Heritage-conversion hotels in secondary cities are drawing operators hunting yield beyond saturated Lisbon and the Algarve.

items.headline: Aura Capital plans a €220M AI data centre in Coruche
items.summary: Aura Technologies will build a 6.4 MW AI data centre at Sorraia Business Park in Santarém, operational by end-2027 and the first in a planned network set to expand into Spain and southern France.
items.why: Digital infrastructure is repricing cheap, gridded land in the Lisbon hinterland — a new competitor for development sites.

items.headline: €25M Aldea Comporta scheme planned for Muda
items.summary: Grupo Nouri will invest €25 million in 21 residential units at Muda, Grândola, with JLL appointed to manage the project — the latest luxury play in the fast-densifying Comporta belt.
items.why: Comporta keeps absorbing capital even as mass-market volumes fall — the top end runs on its own cycle.

items.headline: IMOLEGAL fuses law and engineering under Filipa Arantes Pedroso
items.summary: A new Portuguese real-estate advisory launches combining legal and engineering expertise under one roof, led by Filipa Arantes Pedroso, aimed at a more integrated approach to property projects.
items.why: Integrated legal-technical shops signal a market professionalising around complex, licensing-heavy deals.

items.headline: Inmho and LDC Group complete their merger into one Iberian firm
items.summary: The two residential specialists finish integrating and will now operate as a single organisation across Portugal and Spain, consolidating management and development capacity.
items.why: Scale is consolidating on an Iberian footprint — expect fewer, bigger counterparties on residential platforms.

items.headline: Nine Portuguese projects win at the Architecture MasterPrize 2026
items.summary: Winners span Openbook's 30,000 m² BNP Paribas workplace in Parque das Nações, Atelier Sérgio Rebelo's Douro winery and Plano Humano's scout park — from hillside houses in Braga to interiors on Avenida da Liberdade.
items.why: Design credibility sells space — award-grade architecture is a pricing lever on both offices and villas.

items.headline: OE2027 earmarks €2,003M for housing — and keeps the under-35 IMT break
items.summary: The 2027 budget puts €1,071M into public housing and rehabilitation and €917M into rent support, with the IMT and stamp-duty exemption for first-time buyers under 35 set to continue and €15M to digitise urban licensing.
items.why: State money and faster permitting tilt the field toward affordable and rehab plays — and a continued demand floor under entry-level stock.

items.headline: House prices +18.4% as sales fall 9%, INE confirms
items.summary: Q2 prices rose 18.4% year-on-year to a median €2,445/m² (up 4.6% on Q1), while transactions fell 9% to 37,854 — down in 22 of 26 sub-regions. Médio Tejo (+25.4%) and Oeste (+24.0%) led the gains.
items.why: Price momentum is now driven by scarcity, not demand — underwrite to absorption, not headline appreciation.

items.headline: Portugal M&A bucks the regional boom — deals down 37%
items.summary: Qualifying H1 deals fell 37% to 82, worth roughly €800M, even as capital mobilised across southern Europe rose 37%, per a Forvis Mazars study — though a handful of large deals can swing a small market sharply.
items.why: Thinner deal flow rewards proprietary sourcing — and makes the trophies that do trade a read on where conviction sits.

readForFund.lead: Underwrite the gap, not the trend.
readForFund.text: Prices up 18.4% while volumes fall 9% means pricing power is concentrating in supply-short sub-markets, not rising everywhere.

readForFund.lead: Hospitality is where the money is landing.
readForFund.text: Penha Longa at €140M and Villa Garden's five-star play show international capital still chasing trophy hotels even as broad M&A dries up.

readForFund.lead: Data centres are the new land play.
readForFund.text: Aura's €220M Coruche scheme shows digital-infrastructure demand reaching the Santarém hinterland — cheap, gridded land near Lisbon is being repriced.
OE2027's housing tranche and licensing digitisation favour affordable/rehab plays and faster permitting — a timing signal for developers.

editions.label: 23 Oct
editions.title: Hotels and logistics eat Portugal's real-estate capital as offices and housing investment crater
editions.summary: Where Portugal's real-estate capital goes is shifting fast. In H1 2026, hospitality pulled €508M — up 25% and 37% of all investment — while logistics surged 73%. The flip side is brutal: office investment fell 47% and housing 74%, as buyers chase income and operating upside over development risk. Investment funds now drive 78% of volume — this is an institutional market, not a retail one. Meanwhile the housing crunch deepens: listings fell for a seventh straight quarter and asking prices hit a record €3,228/m². Net: capital is consolidating into hotels, sheds and the funds that own them — and starving the asset classes that actually add new homes.
editions.hook: Portugal's property money is voting with its feet — into hotels and sheds.

items.headline: Montijo's 59,000 m² Logispark changes hands
items.summary: A two-building last-mile logistics complex in Montijo has traded to institutional investors under an exclusive CBRE mandate, with roughly 10,000 m² still available to let. CBRE says it has handled about 60% of Portugal's I&L investment this year — some €200M.
items.why: Prime sheds are scarce, so deals are migrating to secondary hubs like Montijo — where land and forward-funding beat bidding for finished stock.

items.headline: Spain's Aticco buys Lisbon coworking operator Nimbler Spaces
items.summary: Aticco has acquired two recently renovated CBD buildings (7,948 m², 99% occupied) on Duque de Loulé and Fontes Pereira de Melo. The chain will run 16 centres and 87,500 m² across Lisbon, Barcelona and Madrid, with a third Lisbon site opening in Q2.
items.why: Fully-let Lisbon flex assets are now acquisition targets for expanding foreign operators — a vote of confidence in prime-CBD workspace demand.

items.headline: Logistics pipeline tops 1.1M m² for 2026–2029
items.summary: H1 take-up reached about 199,000 m² and prime rents keep rising, says B.Prime, with Sines, the Portos 5+ strategy and rail links underpinning a development wave built around nearshoring, e-commerce and data centres.
items.why: A pipeline that still trails demand means developers who can deliver modern, ESG-compliant space will set rents — the scarcity is the opportunity.

items.headline: State's property sell-off to fund housing has stalled
items.summary: The government planned three 2026 auctions of 16 state buildings to finance housing policy; only one has run, selling three assets for about €21M in March. Thirteen properties — including the Education ministry building — remain unsold, yet the 2027 Budget pencils in €526M of property-sale revenue.
items.why: Public land and stock are a wild card for supply — if the State can't hit its own sales timetable, don't underwrite deals assuming it will.

items.headline: Capital rotates: hotels and logistics up, offices and housing down
items.summary: Portugal drew €1.4bn of real-estate investment in H1 2026, flat on a strong 2025 while Europe fell 23%, per Colliers. Hospitality led at €508M (+25%) and logistics jumped 73%, but offices sank 47% and housing 74% — and funds accounted for 78% of all volume.
items.why: This is a selectivity story, not a capital-shortage one — income-producing assets are winning, and development-heavy bets must price that in.

items.headline: Homes for sale drop 4% — a seventh straight quarterly fall
items.summary: Listings fell 4% year-on-year over the summer, with Funchal (-33%), Porto (-21%) and Faro (-15%) hit hardest. Asking prices rose 7.9% in September to a record median of €3,228/m²; the 6% construction-VAT cut won't bite until new supply lands.
items.why: The supply gap is structural — demand for new build-to-sell and affordable product has a long runway before prices ease.

items.headline: Families' property stock hits €708bn, up ~50% in 15 years
items.summary: Banco de Portugal puts the value of homes held by households at €708bn in 2025, from €473bn in 2010 — mostly price appreciation. Property is still 52% of household assets, and 74% for those below median wealth.
items.why: Housing wealth is deeply concentrated in bricks — a powerful political constraint on any reform that could soften prices.

readForFund.text: Hotels and logistics win capital because they throw off cash flow; pure development plays are being repriced for risk.
With sheds short and listings falling for seven quarters, controlling land or forward-funding beats chasing finished stock.

readForFund.lead: Housing demand has a long runway.
readForFund.text: Record prices and a seventh quarter of shrinking supply mean build-to-sell and affordable product face years of unmet demand.
Its own asset sales are slipping, so public land and stock shouldn't anchor a supply thesis.

editions.label: 22 Oct
editions.title: Portugal homes for sale fall 4% as mortgage rates hit 3.19% — supply squeeze bites
editions.summary: Portugal's housing market is now tightening from both sides at once. Homes listed for sale fell 4% year-on-year in Q3 — the seventh straight quarterly decline. At the same time the average mortgage rate climbed to 3.194% in September and Euribor rose again this week across all tenors. The Banco de Portugal warns the crisis won't be solved from the demand side, and Lisbon has just entered UBS's Global Real Estate Bubble Index. Yet capital keeps arriving: €1.4bn flowed into commercial property in H1, 78% of it through funds. Net: scarce supply and costlier money are propping prices up, not cooling them — and institutional money isn't waiting for a correction.
editions.hook: Portugal's housing squeeze tightens from both sides — less to buy, dearer to borrow.

items.headline: Funds still own the board: €1.4bn into commercial property in H1
items.summary: A Colliers snapshot puts H1 commercial investment at about €1.4bn, with foreign capital at 55% and funds making up 78% of all buyers. Local family offices are stepping into assets the big funds have vacated.
items.why: Institutional and foreign money is the price-setter in Portuguese commercial real estate — and the retreat of some fund buyers is opening a rare window for well-capitalised domestic players.

items.headline: Mortgage rate climbs to 3.194% as Euribor grinds higher
items.summary: INE data show the average housing-loan rate rose again in September, with the typical monthly payment reaching €423 and interest back above half of it. Euribor rose on 21 October to 2.670% (3m), 3.030% (6m) and 3.263% (12m).
items.why: Rising debt costs squeeze buyer affordability and underwriting headroom — a tailwind for cash buyers and equity-heavy structures, a headwind for leveraged acquirers.

items.headline: Listings down 4% for a seventh quarter — and Lisbon joins UBS's bubble index
items.summary: Homes for sale fell 4% year-on-year in Q3, the seventh consecutive quarterly drop, keeping pressure on prices at the affordable end. Lisbon has now entered UBS's Global Real Estate Bubble Index, with real prices up ~7%/year over the decade.
items.why: Chronic undersupply underpins the value case for new delivery, but a bubble-index flag signals stretched valuations — stock selection and entry price now matter more than the rising tide.

items.headline: inHabitus targets 1,080 industrialised homes by 2028
items.summary: The Portuguese industrialised-housing start-up, co-founded by Mário Ferraz, has a first phase of 468 homes — Alfena (79, sold out), Setúbal (136), plus Viseu and Greater Porto (253) — with prices from €139,000, claimed ~24% below market per m².
items.why: Industrialised construction is the clearest path to building mid-market product at a profit in a high-cost market — watch whether the cost claims survive at scale.

items.headline: Loivos 475 opens as a new wine-tourism venue in the Douro
items.summary: A new enoturismo space has opened in the Douro valley, adding to a pipeline of hospitality-led rural investment in Portugal's wine regions.
items.why: Wine-tourism assets convert agricultural land into yielding hospitality — a template for value-add plays in Portugal's premium rural corridors.

items.headline: JLL hands Vítor Dias operations for Project & Development Services across Southern Europe
items.summary: JLL Portugal's COO adds Head of Operations for P&DS and Tétris across Portugal, Spain and Italy, keeping his Lisbon base. He joined JLL in 2019 and became COO in 2024.
items.why: A Lisbon-based lead gaining a three-country remit signals JLL is running Iberia and Italy as one project-delivery market — useful for sponsors coordinating cross-border builds.

items.headline: Ingrid Koeck named CEO of Torel Boutiques
items.summary: After a decade leading marketing and communications at the Portuguese luxury-hotel group, Koeck steps up to chief executive of Torel Boutiques.
items.why: Leadership continuity at a growing boutique-hotel operator matters as hospitality remains Portugal's hottest investment class — operators that can scale brand are prized by capital.

items.headline: Openbook takes an Architecture MasterPrize 2026
items.summary: The Portuguese studio Openbook has been distinguished at the international Architecture MasterPrize 2026, adding to a strong year for Portuguese design on the global stage.
items.why: International design recognition burnishes Portugal's brand with global buyers — award-winning architecture is a real premium lever on prime schemes.

items.headline: State-property auctions stall: only 1 of 3 planned sales went ahead
items.summary: The government planned three 2026 auctions of state property to fund housing, but only March's went ahead, raising ~€21m from three assets. A further 13 properties are authorised for sale, and the 2027 Budget pencils in €526m of disposal revenue.
items.why: A stalled state-disposal pipeline means a big pool of prime public assets stays off-market — but the authorised 13 and the €526m Budget line are a pipeline worth tracking.

items.headline: Affordable-rent caps now live: €224 to €2,066 by municipality and typology
items.summary: A decree in force since 14 October sets maximum affordable rents ranging from €224 to €2,066 depending on location and unit type — and a new working group has been created to draft a national Construction Code.
items.why: Caps define the revenue ceiling on affordable-rent schemes; getting the location-and-typology maths right is now central to underwriting any subsidised product.

readForFund.text: With rates up and a bubble flag on Lisbon, entry price and stress-tested debt carry the deal — not the assumption prices keep rising.
A seventh straight quarterly fall in listings and 78% fund-driven capital keep new, well-located delivery the surest way to meet real demand.
inHabitus's industrialised model points to where margin now lives in mid-market housing — building cheaper, not just selling higher.
Thirteen authorised assets and a €526m disposal line in the 2027 Budget could put prime public real estate in play — if the auctions actually run.

editions.label: 21 Oct
editions.title: Rent-law overhaul slips past November as Chega threatens to tear up its deal
editions.summary: The AD government's rental-market overhaul cleared its first vote on 30 September, but the line-by-line debate won't start until the end of November — after the 2027 state budget. Chega, whose abstention let it through, now says its support is “no blank cheque” and it will vote the changes down unless the bill is fixed. The government has opened the door to the PS, with Housing Minister Miguel Pinto Luz offering a full cross-party debate. With a 180-day drafting window and presidential promulgation still ahead, the final regime may not land before summer 2027. Meanwhile the deals keep moving: the ruined Miramar Hotel site in Cascais sold for €17.4M, and Colliers counted €1.4bn invested in H1. Net: the rules that govern Portuguese rental yields are now a 2027 story — underwrite today's deals on today's law.
editions.hook: Portugal's rental reform is parked in the waiting room until the budget clears.

items.headline: Estoril-Sol sells the ruined Miramar Hotel site in Cascais for €17.4M
items.summary: DTH, a wholly owned Estoril-Sol unit, deeded the 6,046 m² Cascais plot — home to the fire-gutted 1970s hotel — to an undisclosed buyer for €17,397,594, more than double the €8M the group had carried it at. The land is zoned for housing under the 2015 PDM.
items.why: A permitted residential ruin on the Estoril coast clears at 2x book — proof that scarce, licensed land on the Lisbon riviera is repricing hard, right on Verde's doorstep.

items.headline: Square AM eyes €300M of deals in 2026, now backed by Draycott
items.summary: Iberia's largest independent open-ended fund manager expects to close €300M by year-end (€250M in Portugal, €50M in Spain) after Portuguese VC house Draycott bought 100% of it. CEO Nuno Nunes says the firm wants to leave the “second league” for the “first” before 2030.
items.why: Platform consolidation is accelerating — the independents are being bought and scaled, a signal of where fee income and deal flow are concentrating in Iberian funds.

items.headline: Grupo NOURI puts €25M into a 21-home timber scheme in Comporta
items.summary: Aldea Comporta, on a 19-hectare site in Muda, will mix 21 residences — T4 villas with pools plus T2/T3 units — with a club house, sanctuary space and natural pool. AROLLA handles architecture and build in CLT and modular systems; JLL coordinates the project.
items.why: Low-density, timber-built branded residences remain the Comporta playbook — small unit counts, big tickets, and a sustainability story that now sells the sqm.

items.headline: Saraiva Associados turns a two-century Lapa palacete into 12 homes
items.summary: “The Verdian”, on Rua das Janelas Verdes, converts a former bourgeois residence (and 1911–2007 primary school) into eight apartments and four townhouses, T1 to T5+, 91–468 m². Decorated ceilings, stonework and wrought iron are kept against contemporary interiors; developer ReTrend, sold by Sotheby's, finishing September 2028.
items.why: Heritage conversion in prime Lisbon keeps the amenity that new-build can't replicate — and the named-house, gallery-style product is how developers justify the top of the price band.

items.headline: Loulé declares a 'housing emergency' and demands land be freed
items.summary: The Algarve council is pressing for a faster revision of the regional land plan (PROT) and exceptional measures to unlock terrain for affordable housing, warning that current zoning cannot meet demand.
items.why: Municipalities are now the ones pushing to reclassify land — a tailwind for anyone holding, or optioning, developable sites where the PDM/PROT is the binding constraint.

items.headline: Colliers: €1.4bn invested in H1 as hospitality and logistics lead
items.summary: Portugal held H1 volume roughly flat at €1.4bn while Europe fell 23%, Colliers reports. Hospitality took €508M (+25%, ~37% of the total) and logistics €169M (+73%, the fastest-growing segment); offices sank 47% and residential/living fell 74%. Prime yields held steady.
items.why: Capital is rotating decisively into operational, income-producing assets; the plain resi and office trades that defined the last cycle are drying up.

items.headline: Household property wealth up ~50% in 15 years to €708bn
items.summary: Banco de Portugal data show the value of households' real estate rose from €473bn (2010) to €708bn (2025), even as property slipped from 54% to 52% of household assets. For below-median households real estate is ~74% of wealth; for the top 10%, under 40%.
items.why: Portuguese wealth is overwhelmingly bricks — which is exactly why housing is this parliament's hottest political wire and why any rent-law shift moves real money.

items.headline: One in eight homes now sells in under a week
items.summary: idealista data show 12% of homes listed in Q3 2026 went under offer within seven days, with pricing and listing quality driving time on market — a read on just how tight the demand-supply gap has become.
items.why: Velocity like this means the market still clears priced stock fast — exit risk on well-located resi product stays low even as policy noise rises.

readForFund.text: The rental regime is a 2027 story — price deals on the rules in force, not the ones being promised.

readForFund.lead: Follow the capital, not the headlines.
readForFund.text: Foreign money was 55% of H1 volume and funds drove 78% of it — institutional appetite for Portugal is intact.
Hospitality (+25%) and logistics (+73%) took the lion's share of H1; the yield story has moved to operational assets.
From Loulé's “emergency” to Cascais's €17.4M ruin, control of permitted sites is the edge.

editions.label: 20 Oct
editions.title: Portugal holds €1.4bn as Europe sinks 23% — hotels and logistics soak up the capital
editions.summary: Portuguese commercial real estate pulled in €1.4 billion in the first half, flat on a record 2025 even as European volumes fell 23%. The money is rotating hard: hotels took 37% (€508M, up 25%) and logistics surged 73%, while residential collapsed 74% and offices fell 47%. Greater Porto hit a ten-year high of €451M, led by retail and hotels. On the housing side, asking prices set a record €3,228/m² (+7.9% y/y) as for-sale supply fell for a seventh straight quarter and one in eight homes now sells in under a week. And Parliament's rental-law reform cleared its first vote — faster evictions, the 2% rent-increase cap scrapped. Net: the capital is still here and newly selective — chasing income in hospitality and sheds, not housing or offices.
editions.hook: Capital isn't leaving Portugal — it's just changing address.

items.headline: Portugal holds €1.4bn as Europe drops 23% — hotels and logistics soak up the capital
items.summary: Colliers' H1 2026 snapshot puts commercial investment at €1.4bn, level with an exceptional 2025. Hotels led at €508M (37%, +25%), logistics jumped 73% to €169M, while residential sank 74% to €88M and offices fell 47% to €70M.
items.why: Portugal's relative stability versus a sliding Europe is the pitch to cross-border capital — but the rotation says yield-bearing hospitality and logistics win, speculative resi and offices don't.

items.headline: Asking prices hit a record €3,228/m², up 7.9% on the year
items.summary: The idealista index shows September asking prices 7.9% higher year-on-year at an all-time €3,228/m², though the quarterly rise was a modest 0.5%. Lisbon leads at €6,256/m², ahead of Porto (€4,346), Funchal (€4,066) and Faro (€3,924).
items.why: New records with a flattening quarterly curve point to a price plateau at the top — underwriting should lean on income and scarcity, not another leg of headline appreciation.

items.headline: One in eight homes now sells in under a week as supply keeps falling
items.summary: Some 12% of homes listed in Q3 sold within seven days; São Miguel (19%) and Porto (17%) move fastest, Bragança slowest (5%). It lands alongside a 4% year-on-year drop in for-sale listings — the seventh straight quarterly fall, with Funchal down 33% and Porto down 21%.
items.why: A persistent, broad-based supply squeeze is what keeps prices firm despite weaker affordability — it is the structural case for building and holding, not a cyclical blip.

items.headline: Greater Porto investment hits a ten-year record of €451M
items.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's first Market Focus Porto report puts H1 commercial investment at €451M, up 8% and the highest in a decade, led by retail and hotels. Office take-up rose 37% through August with 90,000 m² under development; new store openings grew 50%.
items.why: Porto is no longer the discount alternative to Lisbon — record volumes and a thin modern-space pipeline mean pricing power is moving north.

items.headline: A 200-year-old Lapa palacete becomes The Verdian, 12 new homes
items.summary: On Rua das Janelas Verdes, developer ReTrend is converting a former two-centuries-old school into eight apartments and four townhouses (T1–T5+, 91–335 m²), designed by Saraiva Associados and sold through Portugal Sotheby's. Completion is set for September 2028.
items.why: Heritage conversions in prime Lisbon remain the reliable high-margin play — scarce product, premium buyers, and a design story that sells.

items.headline: Viana do Castelo commits €8.5M to 64 controlled-cost homes
items.summary: The council has approved a contract to build 64 T1–T3 apartments at below-market "controlled costs" for middle-class families in Darque, redeveloping six long-neglected plots. The scheme, launched in 2023, was delayed by land acquisition and a tender challenge.
items.why: Municipal "custos controlados" programmes are becoming a real supply channel — and a template for public-private partnership on the mid-market gap.

items.headline: Logistics pipeline tops 1.1M m² for 2026–29, anchored on Sines
items.summary: A B. Prime study records ~199,000 m² of industrial-and-logistics take-up in H1 and a pipeline above 1.1M m² through 2029, driven by e-commerce, trade reshuffling and Portugal's Atlantic position. The expanding Port of Sines and the Portos 5+ plan sit at the centre.
items.why: Logistics is Portugal's fastest-growing asset class (+73% in H1) but still supply-starved — the gap between a big pipeline and modern stock is where development returns live.

items.headline: Rental-law reform clears its first vote; agent confidence in letting rebounds
items.summary: Parliament's rental reform passed a first vote — faster evictions, scrapping the 2% cap on rent rises, and deposit changes — while a 10% IRS rate on rental income is already in force. The ISSI confidence index for letting rose to 51.6, even as sales confidence fell to a series-low 64.1. Rents were up 6.1% y/y in September.
items.why: Removing the rent cap and speeding evictions materially improves build-to-rent and standing-residential math — but it's still in committee, so model the reversal risk too.

readForFund.text: Capital is paying up for hotels and sheds because they yield; the resi and office collapses show the growth trade is over.
Volumes held flat while Europe fell 23% — that relative stability is itself the headline for cross-border LPs.
A seventh straight drop in listings with prices at record highs means scarcity, not a cycle — it underwrites land and build-to-sell.
A scrapped 2% cap and faster evictions reset BTR returns — model the upside and the political risk of a reversal.

editions.label: 19 Oct
editions.title: Funds grabbed 78% of Portugal's €1.4bn H1 property spend — and most was foreign
editions.summary: Portuguese commercial real estate drew roughly €1.4 billion in the first half of 2026, and the capital behind it is narrowing to a type. Funds supplied 78% of that investment, dwarfing operators (13%), developers (5%) and private buyers (4%). International capital made up 55% of the total, with local family offices filling much of the rest. Colliers reads it as confirmation of Portugal's pull on foreign money — and of domestic players stepping in while some traditional funds sit on the sidelines. The deal flow tells the same story: Barcelona's Aticco bought operator Nimbler Spaces to anchor a Lisbon coworking push, while a Benfica office block is being reborn as 85 apartments. Net: the market is liquid, foreign-led and fund-driven — pricing power sits with whoever can pool patient capital.
editions.hook: Portugal's property market has become a funds' game — and the chips are foreign.

items.headline: Aticco buys Nimbler Spaces to build a Lisbon coworking platform
items.summary: Barcelona-based Aticco acquired one of Portugal's leading coworking operators, taking over two renovated CBD buildings (Marquês and Picoas) totalling 7,948 m² at 99% occupancy. With a third Lisbon asset in works, it will manage 16 centres and 87,500 m² across Iberia; price undisclosed.
items.why: Office-to-coworking consolidation, with 53% of space now on management (not lease) contracts, lets owners share operating upside — a model worth watching as flex demand reprices Lisbon offices.

items.headline: Benfica office block to become 85 apartments in a €50M conversion
items.summary: Family office Mello RDC bought the ~11,000 m² building from Grupo Ageas and will turn it into 85 T1–T3 homes with Monsanto views, at about €6,500/m². Designed by Atelier Posto 9; still in licensing, with construction slated for H2 2027 and completion end-2029.
items.why: Change-of-use from obsolete offices to residential is where Lisbon value is being made — the underwriting skill is licensing risk and construction cost, not land discovery.

items.headline: Viana do Castelo approves €8.5M for 64 controlled-cost homes
items.summary: The municipality awarded the contract for 64 T1–T3 units in Darque aimed at middle-class and young families at below-market rents, part of a local housing strategy that has now committed nearly €51M and reached 641 households, much of it PRR-funded.
items.why: PRR deadlines are pushing municipal supply into the market outside the big cities — a signal of where public co-investment and future rental stock will land.

items.headline: Vanguard's Terraços do Monte crowns a Graça hilltop, by ARX Arquitetos
items.summary: Vanguard Properties is delivering 15 apartments — including two ~330 m² penthouses — across two blocks on the highest point of Rua Damasceno Monteiro, with Tagus views, indoor/outdoor pools, spa and BREEAM certification. ARX Portugal designed it; roughly a third is already sold, with JLL co-marketing and completion due 2028.
items.why: Branded architecture plus sustainability certification is becoming table stakes at Lisbon's prime end — design and ESG credentials now carry the pricing premium.

items.headline: Funds took 78% of H1 investment; 55% of capital was foreign
items.summary: Colliers' Q2 snapshot puts H1 2026 commercial investment near €1.4bn, with funds at 78%, operators 13%, developers 5% and private 4%. International capital was 55%, local family offices much of the rest, as stable prime yields and steadier financing underpin activity.
items.why: A fund-dominated, foreign-led bid sets Portugal's clearing price offshore — domestic buyers compete on access to pooled capital, not just local knowledge.

items.headline: Q3 house prices up 2.3% q/q — but annual growth has halved
items.summary: Confidencial Imobiliário's residential index rose 2.3% in Q3 over Q2 (after 3.5% in Q2), while year-on-year growth cooled to 14.5% from 21.7% a year earlier — a 7.2-point deceleration on the national mainland index.
items.why: Prices are still rising, but the pace is normalising — base cases built on 20%+ appreciation need a reset toward low-teens.

items.headline: 83% of Portuguese retail property investors reinvest their gains
items.summary: On crowdfunding platform wecity, 83% of Portuguese investors have reinvested at least once, spreading about €4,000 across five projects; 15% are under 30, and Porto is the favourite domestic city — a growing Iberian retail-capital habit.
items.why: Retail capital is becoming stickier and more diversified — a widening pool that fractional and fund vehicles can tap as institutional tickets get scarcer.

readForFund.text: With funds taking 78% of H1 volume, deals flow to whoever aggregates patient money — the structural tailwind behind a vehicle like Verde 2050.
At 55% international capital, Portugal's bid is set offshore — a European allocation shift moves prices as much as local rates do.
Benfica offices → 85 homes, Graça's hilltop revival: value is being created by repositioning tired stock, so underwrite change-of-use and licensing, not just land.
Resi still rose 2.3% q/q but annual growth halved to 14.5%; plan entries on normalising appreciation, not another 20% year.

editions.label: 18 Oct
editions.title: Bank of Portugal: demand-side housing fixes just push prices higher
editions.summary: A new study from Banco de Portugal delivers an awkward verdict: demand-side housing measures — buyer subsidies, tax breaks, cheaper credit — mainly push up prices and rents, not access. The bank finds demand shocks lift home values more as financial assets than as places to rent, widening the price-to-rent gap. That lands just as OE2027 doubles down on demand relief — a higher IMT Jovem ceiling and a bigger rent deduction. The implied fix is supply, which the budget also funds but which takes years to arrive. For now, the subsidies risk inflating the very assets they target. Net: the policy tailwind investors have priced in may be propping up values more than affordability — underwrite scarcity, not stimulus.
editions.hook: Portugal's central bank says you can't subsidise your way out of a housing crisis.

items.headline: Tupperware's former Montalvo factory fails to sell at auction
items.summary: The ex-Tupperware plant in Montalvo (Constância) drew no buyer; the leading bids came in well below creditors' reference values, so the offers will be reassessed rather than awarded.
items.why: Large single-use industrial sites are hard to clear at book — price repositioning and demolition risk into any distressed-asset bid, not the headline reserve.

items.headline: Logicor to replace an obsolete platform with 34,000 m² of Class A logistics
items.summary: Logicor will demolish an outdated facility on a 66,000 m² site in Póvoa de Santa Iria and build 34,000 m² of modern Class A logistics space on the northern edge of Lisbon.
items.why: Redevelopment, not greenfield, is how prime logistics gets delivered where land is scarce — brownfield near the capital is the input driving rental growth.

items.headline: Palm Luxury Living brings four detached villas to Carcavelos
items.summary: A new scheme in Carcavelos offers four T4 detached houses with minimalist design and energy-efficient specs, on the Cascais line just west of Lisbon.
items.why: The Lisbon–Cascais coast keeps absorbing low-density luxury — small, high-ticket villa plays are where pricing power is firmest in Verde's home corridor.

items.headline: Almora Melides adds 22 houses on the Alentejo coast
items.summary: A new 22-house development totalling about 2,300 m² of construction is rising in the historic centre of Melides, the Alentejo coastal village increasingly billed as the next Comporta.
items.why: Melides is the frontier of the Comporta luxury thesis — early, low-density product tests how far second-home demand will travel down the coast.

items.headline: Grupo Casais opens a construction-tech hub in Braga
items.summary: The Casais group launched a Braga technology hub focused on digital coordination, off-site production and industrialised building components, part of its push to modernise how it builds.
items.why: Portugal's big contractors are betting on industrialised construction to beat labour shortages and cost inflation — delivery capacity, not just capital, is becoming the differentiator.

items.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo backs a €20M water-bottling plant in Bragança
items.summary: A company jointly owned by Grupo Outeirinho and Cristiano Ronaldo is building a water-bottling factory costing nearly €20M in the village of Gostei, Bragança — a rare industrial bet on Portugal's interior.
items.why: Name-backed industrial investment in the low-density interior is a reminder that capital — and jobs — are spreading beyond the coastal metros, seeding future demand.

items.headline: A Portuguese-Norwegian partnership bets on mass-timber building
items.summary: A Portuguese firm signed a strategic partnership through 2030 with a Norwegian timber-engineering specialist, announced at the Wood Giants congress, to advance engineered-timber construction in Portugal.
items.why: Mass timber is moving from showcase to supply chain — a route to faster, lower-carbon builds that can command a sustainability premium with institutional buyers.

items.headline: Minister denies the new urban-rehabilitation regime was 'made to measure'
items.summary: Infrastructure and Housing Minister Miguel Pinto Luz rejected claims that Portugal's revised urban-rehabilitation rules were written to suit him, and offered to explain the regime to Parliament.
items.why: The rehab regime underpins value-add underwriting — political noise around it is worth tracking, because any wobble in the rules changes the maths on refurbishing older stock.

items.headline: Homes for sale fall 4% — a seventh straight quarterly drop
items.summary: idealista data show the stock of homes for sale in Portugal fell about 4% year-on-year in Q3 2026, the seventh consecutive quarterly decline, keeping upward pressure on prices.
items.why: Shrinking resale supply is the structural floor under Portuguese prices — and the clearest evidence for the central bank's point that the shortage sits on the supply side.

readForFund.lead: Supply, not subsidy, is the thesis.
readForFund.text: The Bank of Portugal and a seventh straight supply drop point the same way — bet on scarcity of product, not on demand-side stimulus that mostly lifts prices.
Logicor's Póvoa redevelopment shows the only way to add prime logistics near Lisbon is to replace obsolete stock — scan for change-of-use and demolition plays on serviced land.
Carcavelos villas and Melides houses confirm low-density luxury on the Lisbon–Alentejo littoral holds pricing power — small tickets, high margins, Verde's home turf.

readForFund.lead: Delivery capacity is the new moat.
readForFund.text: Casais's industrialised-build hub and the mass-timber tie-up signal that whoever builds faster and cheaper wins — back operators, not just assets.

editions.label: 17 Oct
editions.title: Funds take 78% of Portugal's €1.4bn property investment — foreign money back on top
editions.summary: Funds drove 78% of Portugal's real estate investment in the first half of 2026, Colliers data shows. Total volume reached about €1.4 billion, with international capital at 55% and domestic family offices taking much of the rest. The structural read: Portugal now trades like an institutional market, not a buy-a-villa story. Meanwhile Parliament's NRAU overhaul — faster evictions, no 2% cap on new-contract rents — cleared a first vote and sits in committee. And logistics is the quiet winner, with a 1.1 million m² pipeline through 2029. Net: capital is flowing and rules are tightening — the edge now is in sourcing, not discovery.
editions.hook: Portugal's property market is a funds game now — and the capital is mostly foreign.

items.headline: Confrasilvas buys Boavista's Estádio do Bessa for €33m
items.summary: Lisbon real estate group Confrasilvas, owned by the Maurício family, will acquire the Bessa stadium and sports complex after the bankrupt club's creditors approved its bid on 14 October, clearing the €32.92m auction floor. The group is eyeing a mixed housing-and-retail scheme on the 21,000+ m² plot.
items.why: Distressed-sport real estate is becoming a repositioning play — a landmark urban plot acquired below book and primed for mixed-use density.

items.headline: Estoril-Sol sells former Hotel Miramar land for €17.3m
items.summary: The casino group has offloaded the plot of the old Miramar hotel on the Estoril coast for €17.3 million, releasing a prime seafront site into the development pipeline.
items.why: Scarce Linha de Cascais seafront land rarely trades — a price benchmark for anyone underwriting the Estoril–Cascais corridor.

items.headline: Mello RDC turns a Benfica office block into 85 homes
items.summary: Family office Mello RDC, led by António Ribeiro da Cunha, is converting a former office building into "Panorama" — 85 flats (T1–T3) across ~11,000 m², a €50m investment with a €6,500/m² reference price. Pending Lisbon council licensing; build slated for H2 2027 to end-2029.
items.why: Office-to-resi conversion is live in secondary Lisbon — a template for repricing obsolete stock into mid-market housing.

items.headline: Grupo NOURI's €25m "Aldea Comporta" lands in Muda
items.summary: A €25m, 21-home scheme on 19 hectares near Comporta — T4 villas with pools down to T2/T3 residences, plus a clubhouse and natural pool — developed by Grupo NOURI, with AROLLA on architecture and JLL on project management.
items.why: The Comporta luxury-second-home thesis keeps absorbing capital — low density, high ticket, and a JLL/architect pairing signalling institutional polish.

items.headline: NRAU rental-law overhaul clears first vote
items.summary: Parliament approved the government's urban-leasing revision in principle on 30 September; it is now in committee. The draft ends the 2% cap on new-contract rents (with income/age exceptions), lets landlords evict after two months' arrears instead of three, and allows three months' advance rent.
items.why: A landlord-friendlier regime would lift achievable rents and cut void risk — materially improving the case for build-to-rent underwriting.

items.headline: New 2026 capital-gains coefficients published
items.summary: Portaria n.º 457/2026/1 (Diário da República, 15 Oct) sets the currency-devaluation coefficients that adjust a property's acquisition price when computing taxable gains on 2026 sales — directly shaping IRS due on disposals.
items.why: A small input that moves net proceeds — refresh exit models for any 2026 disposal before signing.

items.headline: Funds took 78% of H1 investment; foreign capital leads
items.summary: Colliers' Q2 snapshot puts H1 2026 commercial investment near €1.4bn, with funds at 78% of volume, international capital at 55% and domestic family offices prominent in the remainder. Operators (13%), promoters (5%) and private investors (4%) round it out.
items.why: Pricing is set by institutional money — to compete, match their cost of capital or win on off-market sourcing.

items.headline: Portugal climbs the global logistics radar
items.summary: A B. Prime report flags Portugal's gateway location, e-commerce growth and supply-chain resilience demand: ~199,000 m² absorbed in H1 2026, a 2026–2029 pipeline above 1.1 million m², and prime rents still rising, with data centres and last-mile in focus.
items.why: Industrial & logistics is Portugal's structural growth leg — rising rents plus a deep pipeline point to durable income, not a cycle blip.

readForFund.text: With funds at 78% of volume, the only reliable alpha left is off-market origination, not buying what's listed.
Uncapping new-contract rents and faster evictions would lift net yields — model the committee outcome into any build-to-rent case.
Benfica's €6,500/m² office-to-resi shows obsolete stock repricing into mid-market housing — scan for licensable change-of-use.
A 1.1M m² pipeline with rising prime rents is the steadiest cash-flow leg in the Portuguese market right now.

editions.label: 16 Oct
editions.title: Funds drove 78% of Portugal's €1.4bn H1 property spend — hotels and retail took two-thirds
editions.summary: Funds now drive 78% of real-estate investment in Portugal. Colliers counts ~€1.4bn deployed in H1 2026 — flat on last year, but far more concentrated. Hotels (€508m) and retail (€422m) soaked up two-thirds of it; logistics took €169m, living just €88m and offices €70m. Foreign capital led at 55%, though Portuguese family offices are stepping in as some international funds pull back. Beneath the headline calm, the money is quietly picking its spots. Net: capital is abundant but selective — the scarce thing is institutional-grade product, not buyers.
editions.hook: Portugal's capital is pooling into funds — and into hotels and shops.

items.headline: CBRE sells the 59,000 m² Logispark complex in Montijo
items.summary: Two last-mile logistics assets in the Lisbon metro area changed hands, with CBRE as exclusive adviser; ~10,000 m² remains available to let. Buyer and price undisclosed.
items.why: CBRE says it has handled ~60% of Portugal's industrial & logistics volume this year (~€200m) — and institutions are now reaching past prime for scarce big-box product.

items.headline: Aticco buys Nimbler Spaces, taking on ~16,000 m² of Lisbon coworking
items.summary: The flex-office operator absorbs Nimbler's Lisbon portfolio, consolidating a fragmented coworking market as Savills also relocates its Porto office to VIVA Offices.
items.why: Flex continues to consolidate under larger platforms — a signal that occupier demand for serviced space is deep enough to support scale operators, not just one-off floors.

items.headline: Grupo NOURI unveils a €25m, timber-built resort in Comporta
items.summary: Aldea Comporta puts 21 homes — T4 villas with pools plus T2/T3 residences — across 4,700 m² on a 19-hectare Muda estate, using cross-laminated timber and modular systems. AROLLA designs and builds; JLL manages delivery.
items.why: Low-density, CLT-led luxury is becoming the Comporta playbook — proof that premium buyers will pay for sustainability credentials and scarcity, not density.

items.headline: LDC Group and inmho merge into an Iberian condo-management giant
items.summary: Portugal's LDC Group (Loja do Condomínio) and Spain's inmho combine ~24,000 condominiums, ~2,500 staff and roughly 1m clients. Antonio Baldellou leads the new group; LDC's Pedro Pinheiro stays on as Portugal property-management director.
items.why: Property and condo management is institutionalising fast (LDC sits inside Sweden's Odevo) — recurring-fee platforms are quietly becoming an investable asset class of their own.

items.headline: Inês Carneiro wins the Fernando Távora Prize
items.summary: The architect takes one of Portugal's most prestigious research awards for a project on "Arquiteturas do Cosmos," continuing the prize's tradition of funding exploratory travel and thinking.
items.why: Portugal's design reputation is a quiet asset for developers — the architects winning today are the names that sell schemes tomorrow.

items.headline: A Portuguese studio puts AI into architectural plan review
items.summary: Atelier Segmento Urbano launched an AI-assisted service that screens architectural projects for errors and compliance issues before they reach the câmara.
items.why: Anything that de-risks municipal approval shortens the single most unpredictable line in a development schedule — and licensing delay is where Portuguese projects bleed time and money.

items.headline: Government launches a working group to draft a single Construction Code
items.summary: Despacho 12528/2026 (Diário da República, 15 Oct) creates a team — IMPIC, LNEC and Construção Pública, chaired by the Housing Secretary of State's office — to consolidate Portugal's scattered building law into one code under the "Construir Portugal" plan.
items.why: A coherent code could eventually cut the legal uncertainty and cross-referencing that slows every licence — the most consequential structural reform for developers now on the table.

items.headline: PJ raids 53 sites over a €66m IMT-exemption fraud
items.summary: Investigators allege shell companies shuttled property between themselves at token prices to win IMT exemptions, then sold on — including bank portfolios — costing the state €66m+ over 2017–2025. Searches hit homes, banks and a law firm in Lisbon, Porto and Setúbal.
items.why: Expect tighter scrutiny of IMT exemptions and corporate-wrapper deals — the structures used to defer transfer tax are now firmly in the authorities' sights.

items.headline: Funds took 78% of a €1.4bn H1 investment market
items.summary: Colliers' Q2 snapshot puts H1 2026 volume at ~€1.4bn, flat year-on-year. Hotels (€508m) and retail (€422m) led; logistics €169m, living €88m, offices €70m. Foreign capital was 55%, with family offices filling gaps left by retreating international funds.
items.why: The weight in hotels and retail, and the thinness in living and offices, shows where institutional appetite — and pricing tension — actually sits right now.

items.headline: Asking prices up 3.4% in Q3 — but homes take 25% longer to sell
items.summary: Doutor Finanças' observatory puts national asking prices at €3,666/m² (+3.4% in Q3), reversing Q2's dip. Average time to sell an apartment jumped 25% to 132 days; Lisbon is dearest at €5,582/m², though down 1.4%.
items.why: Prices and clearing speed are diverging — sellers keep marking up while buyers take longer, a classic late-cycle gap that rewards patient, well-priced product.

readForFund.lead: Scarcity is on the sell side.
readForFund.text: With funds pushing €1.4bn into a market short of institutional-grade stock, the edge is originating product others can't — the back-the-expert thesis, exactly.
Capital reaching into Montijo for last-mile space says prime yields are compressing beyond the core — second-tier corridors are where value still sits.
A single code replacing scattered building law could cut entitlement risk and timelines — a structural tailwind worth following from despacho to draft.
Asking prices up 3.4% while time-to-sell climbs 25% to 132 days: the list-to-clearing gap is widening — model the exit, not the headline growth.

editions.label: 15 Oct
editions.title: Hotels take €508M, logistics +73%: Portugal's property capital rotates as volumes dip 13%
editions.summary: Portuguese commercial real estate drew €1.378 billion in H1 2026 — down 12.8% year-on-year, but a far milder slide than Europe's 23% drop. Hotels led the pack with €508M, up 25%, now 37% of all capital deployed. Industrial and logistics was the fastest-growing segment, up 73%. Retail fell roughly 30% as buyers turned selective. International investors still drive the market at around 55% of volume. Meanwhile Porto quietly hit a decade-high, and Lisbon put €60M of land on the block. Net: capital isn't leaving Portugal — it's moving to where occupancy and scarcity are, and away from where they aren't.
editions.hook: Portugal's property money is rotating — into hotels and sheds, out of shops.

items.headline: Boavista's Bessa stadium sells for €33M to the builders of Benfica's arena
items.summary: Frozenspark, part of the Confrasilvas group (the Maurício family behind Benfica's stadium), won creditor approval to buy the bankrupt club's Bessa stadium for €33M, just above the €32.92M floor. The site spans ~78,000 m² of built area plus a 21,000+ m² sports complex, with housing-and-commerce redevelopment flagged as possible.
items.why: A distressed sports asset with ~100,000 m² of central-Porto land, bought by an experienced stadium developer — a rare large-scale redevelopment play in a supply-starved city.

items.headline: Lisbon puts 10 municipal plots worth €60M up for public auction
items.summary: The city council will auction ten plots totalling ~30,000 m² on 10 December, with a combined base value near €60M — led by sites in Penha de França (€13.7M), Marvila (€11.9M) and Campolide (€10.9M). Proceeds fund the council's investment plan through 2030.
items.why: Rare prime development land coming to market in a city where buildable plots — not capital — are the scarce input, and a fresh price benchmark for developers.

items.headline: Hotels take €508M as commercial volumes dip 13% — and logistics jumps 73%
items.summary: Colliers' H1 2026 snapshot puts total commercial investment at €1.378bn, down 12.8% but well ahead of Europe's 23% fall. Hotels led at €508M (+25%, 37% of the market); industrial & logistics grew fastest at +73% to €169M; retail slipped ~30% to €422M. Foreign capital is ~55% of the total.
items.why: The capital map is rotating — underwrite hotels and logistics on occupancy and scarcity, and treat retail as an asset-level, not sector-level, bet.

items.headline: Greater Porto hits a decade-high €451M as office take-up jumps 37%
items.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's first Porto market report logs €451M of commercial investment in H1, up 8% and a ten-year record. Office take-up rose 37% through August with 90,000+ m² in the pipeline; retail openings climbed 50%; logistics demand outruns a shortage of modern space. Valongo, Trofa, Santo Tirso and Santa Maria da Feira are emerging as hubs.
items.why: Porto is outrunning the national trend — a decade-high for capital and the strongest office demand in years, concentrated in prime, sustainable stock.

items.headline: House prices rebound 3.4% to €3,666/m² — but Lisbon cools and sales drag
items.summary: Doutor Finanças' Observatório puts advertised prices up 3.4% in Q3 to a €3,666/m² national average, recovering from a Q2 dip. But Lisbon fell 1.4% (still €5,582/m²) while Viseu led at +12.5%, and the average apartment now takes 132 days to sell — up 25%. Rents were flat at €15.48/m², with Lisbon down 5.4%.
items.why: Prices still climb nationally while Lisbon cools and selling times stretch — the market is bifurcating by geography and price band, rewarding disciplined entry.

items.headline: Logistics pipeline tops 1.1M m² through 2029 as Portugal lands on the global radar
items.summary: B. Prime's Prime Mile report records ~199,000 m² of H1 industrial & logistics take-up and a 2026–2029 pipeline expected to exceed 1.1M m², with prime rents still rising. The drivers: e-commerce, the Port of Sines and Portos 5+ plan, rail upgrades, and data-centre demand.
items.why: A 1.1M m² pipeline signals logistics is institutionalising — yet a shortage of modern space keeps pushing prime rents up.

items.headline: Government targets a full inventory of all state-owned property by 2030
items.summary: The 2027 State Budget proposal (OE2027), now before Parliament, sets a 2030 deadline to catalogue every state-owned asset — including properties assigned to third parties and those still misregistered to private owners or extinct entities. The third phase runs 2027–2030 and feeds a full accounting inventory.
items.why: A complete state asset register is the precursor to disposals and public-private deals — a potentially large future pipeline of public land and buildings.

items.headline: Four Portuguese projects make the Dezeen Awards 2026 shortlist
items.summary: From 152 shortlisted projects across 36 countries: Casa Plaj by Extrastudio (House, rural), Mercado do Bairro Padre Cruz by REDO architects (Civic), the Canning Factory by OODA (Heritage), and Casa Sem Pele by Didier Faustino (Small Project). Winners are announced 16 November at London's Royal Opera House.
items.why: Heritage conversions and civic-market regeneration are exactly the adaptive-reuse plays drawing investor capital — and Portuguese studios are setting the template.

readForFund.text: Hotels (+25%) and logistics (+73%) are where occupancy and scarcity live; retail (−30%) needs asset-level conviction, not beta.
A decade-high €451M and +37% office take-up say the second city is no longer the discount play.
Lisbon's €60M auction and Boavista's ~100,000 m² prove buildable plots, not capital, are the scarce input.
A 2030 inventory of public property is the leading indicator of the next wave of disposals and PPP land.
